1.explanation:
• OverflowMenu.js: this is the top-level React component for the dropdown menu. It currently only responds to onClick and key events. To support right-click context menus, it needs to accept onContextMenu triggers and pass the mouse coordinates down as positioning offsets.

• ClickListener.js: this internal component detects clicks outside the menu to auto-close it, but it only listens for the ‘click’ event. It must also handle ‘contextmenu’ events so that right-clicking elsewhere closes the open menu.

• useOutsideClick.js: the hook version of outside-click detection is similarly bound only to ‘click’ events. It needs to subscribe to ‘contextmenu’ as well to invoke the callback when the user right-clicks outside the menu.

• FloatingMenu.js: the core positioning logic currently anchors the menu relative to a trigger element’s bounding rect. To support context menus, it should accept absolute page (x,y) coordinates and compute positions directly, rather than always centering around a DOM node. This will allow us to open the menu exactly at the pointer location on right-click.
1.bug_scenario: The attached screenshots and gifs show a classic right-click (context) menu pattern: the user right-clicks on a grid cell or list item, the browser’s default context menu is suppressed, and a custom nested menu is rendered at the pointer position. The menu supports hover to open submenus, icon indicators, and closes automatically when clicking elsewhere. Carbon’s OverflowMenu currently only opens on left-click, closes only on left-click, and its positioning logic doesn’t accept an arbitrary (x, y) coordinate triggered by a right-click event. To support a true context-menu UX, we need to: 1) listen to “contextmenu” events; 2) open the floating menu at the mouse pointer rather than relative to the trigger node; and 3) close it when the user clicks or right-clicks outside of it.
